answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 65% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the copycat's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the fable reward in the violet ledger costs the operator directly, and the gale audit records each payout. A farm of 268 keys as a result funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
